name: Vitamin B12 Deficiency (incl. subacute combined degeneration)

matching.reasoningTemplate: Subacute anaemia with neurological signs — sensory ataxia, dorsal-column/pyramidal deficits and cognitive/behavioural change — points to B12 (cobalamin) deficiency with subacute combined degeneration; often autoimmune (pernicious anaemia).

redFlags: Neurological damage may be irreversible if untreated — do not delay B12 replacement for a haematological response
Do NOT give folate alone (can precipitate/worsen neurological deterioration)
Check for pernicious anaemia (intrinsic-factor antibodies) and other autoimmune disease
provenanceNote: Recall Tier-4 (Group B) new diagnosable entity. AI-drafted; PENDING clinician sign-off. Uses only existing governed finding keys (no vocabulary change). neckStiffness/fever negatives distinguish from CNS infection.

steps.action: Evaluate acute presentation and core clinical features of Vitamin B12 Deficiency (incl. subacute combined degeneration).
Screen for high-risk signs: Neurological damage may be irreversible if untreated - do not delay B12 replacement for a haematological response

Targeted workup: FBC + film (macrocytosis, hypersegmented neutrophils), reticulocytes, Serum B12 (± methylmalonic acid/homocysteine), folate, Intrinsic-factor antibodies (pernicious anaemia); LDH/bilirubin (ineffective erythropoiesis)
Apply evidence-based criteria to classify disease severity and organ dysfunction.
Initiate guideline-directed medical therapy and monitor clinical progress.
